findings.title: Index/lifecycle init failure now aborts server construction (and therefore process startup)
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns the error. Previously initialization was lazy, so a failure only broke the individual gRPC call that triggered it. Now any failure in `lifecycle.Init`, `search.init` (which lists all resource stats and builds every index), or `initWatcher` makes the constructor fail, which propagates up through DI and prevents the storage server / Grafana from starting at all. This is a real, reachable scenario: for file-backed bleve indexes `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:98) returns `ErrorIndexPathExists` when the directory from a previous run is still on disk (the code itself has a TODO about not yet checking the persisted RV), and transient DB errors during `GetResourceStats` have the same effect. Startup also now blocks for the full duration of indexing all namespaces. Consider keeping init asynchronous/retryable, or at least making index build failures non-fatal.

findings.title: cancel() is not called when Init fails in NewResourceServer, leaking goroutines
findings.body: The cancelable context created at line 229 is only cancelled via `server.Stop`. On the new error path (`err := s.Init(ctx); if err != nil { return nil, err }`), the constructor returns without calling `cancel()`, so the context (and anything already started under it) is leaked. This matters because `search.init` may already have called `storage.WatchWriteEvents` and started the SQL poller/event-handling goroutines before the error occurred; nothing will ever stop them, and the caller has no handle to the server to call `Stop`. Call `cancel()` (and ideally `lifecycle.Stop`) before returning the error.

findings.title: Removing per-request Init() checks makes the shutdown guard dead code
findings.body: `Stop` sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" / "service is stopped", which used to be surfaced to clients because every handler started with `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { return nil, err }`. All of those checks were removed in this diff, so no handler ever reads `initErr` again. After `Stop()` has cancelled the background context and the backend lifecycle has shut down, Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search now proceed into a stopped backend instead of returning a clear "service is stopping" error, producing confusing driver-level errors (or worse, work against a closed DB). Either keep a lightweight state check in the handlers or remove the now-misleading `initErr` assignments in `Stop`.

findings.title: Data race on shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` in searchSupport.init
findings.body: Inside `group.Go(...)` the closure writes the function-scoped `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments `totalBatchesIndexed++`. With `group.SetLimit(s.initWorkers)` these closures run concurrently, so both are unsynchronized writes from multiple goroutines: a genuine data race (the race detector will flag it), an undercounted `namespaced_indexed` span attribute, and — worse — error misattribution: one goroutine can overwrite `err` with `nil` before another returns it (swallowing a build failure) or a goroutine can return an error produced by a different build. Since init failure now aborts server startup (server.go:258), a spuriously propagated error can block the whole process. Use a local `err :=` inside the closure and an atomic/counter for the batch count.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads b.cache without holding cacheMu — concurrent map read/write panic
findings.body: `TotalDocs()` iterates `b.cache` with no lock, while `BuildIndex` now writes the map (line 138) outside any long-held lock, from the N concurrent index-build workers and from lazy builds triggered by search/watch events. A concurrent map read and map write is a fatal runtime panic in Go (not just a benign race), taking down the process. This path is newly exercised by the `s.search.TotalDocs()` call added in search.go:216 and by any metric/diagnostic caller. Take `cacheMu.RLock()` in `TotalDocs` (and avoid holding it while calling `index.DocCount()` if that is expensive, e.g. snapshot the slice of indexes first).

findings.title: Dropping the BuildIndex-wide lock allows concurrent duplicate builds of the same key
findings.body: The write lock that previously covered the whole of `BuildIndex` is now only taken around the cache assignment. `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` does a lock-free `GetIndex` followed by `build`, so two concurrent requests (or a watch event plus a search) for the same NamespacedResource can now execute `BuildIndex` for the same key at the same time. Consequences: (a) for file-backed indexes both goroutines call `bleve.New` on the identical directory `Root/namespace/resource.group`, which at best fails with ErrorIndexPathExists and at worst leaves two writers on the same on-disk index; (b) both perform a full re-list/re-index of the resource (wasted DB and CPU work); (c) the loser's index object silently overwritten in the cache is never closed, leaking its file handles/memory, while callers that already got the old handle keep searching a discarded index. Finer-grained locking is fine, but it needs to be per-key (e.g. a per-key build mutex or singleflight) rather than removed.

findings.title: BuildIndex still discards the span context, so the indexing work is not under its span
findings.body: This PR's stated goal includes fixing trace propagation (`ctx, span := ...` in search.go and sql/backend.go), but `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` still uses `_, span := b.tracer.Start(ctx, ...)` and never passes the derived context anywhere. The `builder(idx)` callback executed at line 126 captures the caller's context instead, so all the list/iterate/document-build spans produced during the actual indexing attach to the parent `unified_search.Build` span rather than to `unified_search.bleve.BuildIndex`, leaving BuildIndex as an empty leaf span and making it impossible to attribute index build time in traces.

findings.title: Storage-server integration test silently disabled for postgres in CI
findings.body: The only integration test that boots the `StorageServer` module target is now skipped for postgres with the comment "test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally." This PR moves unified storage initialization (index build, watcher start) into `NewResourceServer`, i.e. into module startup — exactly the code path this test exercises — so disabling it removes CI coverage of the change for one of the supported databases and hides whatever failure prompted the skip (it may well be caused by this PR's startup-blocking init rather than by Drone). The root cause should be identified before the skip is merged, or the skip should link to a tracking issue with the observed failure.
